Repeated configuration and safeguard descriptions do not resolve those questions. Useful bounded reasoning merits 2, but the response does not demonstrate the decision-targeted prioritization required for 3. No retrieval was available, so the absence of reads itself is not penalized.

experiment_quality.rationale: There is a historical baseline comparator, consistent preprocessing, isolated execution, independent technician-reported misses, conditional time splitting, asset slices, resource metrics and positive/negative/inconclusive decisions. Importantly, recall is explicitly limited to technician and historical targets, not claimed to represent full coverage. This meets 2. It lacks a representative search for misses outside all candidate sets, source slices, per-pass marginal coverage, final-entity correctness metrics, validated historical truth, uncertainty estimates and update dependency-closure/replay testing. A held-out update month also does not specify the full reference/index workload. Thus it falls short of the comprehensive falsifiable entity-centered experiment required for 3.

This merits 2. It does not explain how input-order truncation discards true matches despite an uncapped pass union, how candidate-distribution changes invalidate the pre-cap calibration, or how false merges and corrections affect entity history and update closure. Reversibility is a generic rollback instruction rather than a concrete history-preserving mechanism, precluding 3.

technical_reasoning.rationale: Basic blocking, ANN and cross-encoder roles and compute tradeoffs are plausible, and the cap is correctly recognized as a recall problem. However, the mechanism remains mostly generic: no treatment of arbitrary input ordering or loss of uncapped union coverage, namespace/placeholder eligibility, targeted multi-pass skew handling, adaptive selective scoring, or distribution-induced invalidation of existing calibration. The proposed candidate set is simply handed to an assumed existing resolution engine without entity/master/history contracts or incremental replay effects. These are important assumptions and pipeline interactions, not minor omissions, so the response meets 1 rather than 2 or 3. It neither guarantees capped recall nor endorses unguarded exhaustive scoring.
